resultText:
Good, `includeBoundTextElement` is optional, so the change is valid.

**Root cause:** In `actionToggleLinearEditor.perform` (`packages/excalidraw/actions/actionLinearEditor.tsx`), the selected element was fetched with `includeBoundTextElement: true` and then indexed with `[0]`. `getSelectedElements` iterates the scene's elements in their document (z-index) order, pushing both the selected arrow and its bound text child into the result array in whatever order they appear in that document. In most documents the arrow precedes its bound text, so `[0]` was the arrow — but in documents where the bound text element happens to be ordered before its container arrow, `[0]` was the text element instead. That text element's `id` then failed the invariant check against `appState.selectedLinearElement.elementId` (which is always set to the arrow's id), triggering the crash — hence it depended on the document, not the arrow itself.

**Fix:** Dropped `includeBoundTextElement: true` from that lookup, since `selectedElementIds` already contains only the arrow when it's selected (the `predicate` and label/`PanelComponent` functions in the same file already do a plain lookup without that option). This makes the fetch order-independent and matches the rest of the action, without touching the predicate or line-editing behavior for arrows that already worked.

This doesn't change when the action is offered (the `predicate` is untouched) or how line editing behaves for arrows where it already worked (in those cases `selectedElements[0]` was already the arrow, `includeBoundTextElement` was a no-op there). It only removes the faulty lookup that could resolve to the bound text element instead of the arrow.

Fixed `packages/excalidraw/actions/actionLinearEditor.tsx:55-59`. The crash happened because `getSelectedElements` was asked to include the bound text element, and when a document's z-order history placed that text before its container arrow in the elements array, `[0]` picked the text element instead of the arrow — tripping the `elementId` mismatch invariant. Since only the arrow is ever selected here, dropping `includeBoundTextElement: true` fixes it without touching predicate or editing behavior.
